name: matching: Lesson 15.6 summarized guidelines for data scientists on what…
questionText: Lesson 15.6 summarized guidelines for data scientists on what sorts of variables to include or exclude in fitting multiple regression models. Which of the following guidelines is accurate with respect to variables that we generally want to INCLUDE as predictors?

blanks.label: It is essential to incorporate variables that are correlated with both the outcome (Y) and the particular X predictor of interest.
It is beneficial, but not strictly essential, to include variables that are correlated with Y even if they are not correlated with a particular X predictor of interest.
Always include an interaction term for two X predictors if those predictors are both main effects in the model.
Failing to include an important confounder as a model predictor could lead to “omitted-variable bias.”
"Colliders" should be predictors in the model if they can be identified and reliably measured.

name: multiple_dropdowns: This is one of multiple questions about the same…
questionText: This is one of multiple questions about the same scenario. NCAA coaches may be compensated with salary as well as with an annual bonus. The amount of that bonus may be contingent on team performance as well as meeting off-field thresholds with respect to players' grades and conduct. The distribution of salary and bonus is something that coaches negotiate with the Athletic Director at a NCAA school. A college football coach-who-will-not-be-named is evaluating the job market and wants to predict what sort of bonus compensation he might expect to earn at various NCAA schools. Using NCAA Salaries data, he fits a model with the following variables: Bonus: maximum annual bonus (in millions of dollars) Salary: annual salary (in millions of dollars) SEC: whether the school is in the Southeastern Conference (SEC = 1) or not (SEC = 0) The model equation is: Bonus=0.45+0.15∗Salary+0.84∗SEC−0.11∗(Salary∗SEC) Use this model equation to fill in the blanks below with the best option: At SEC schools, maximum bonuses are [ Select ] ["lower", "higher"] by about [ Select ] ["$840,000", "$730,000", "$990,000", "$450,000", "$150,000"] relative to non-SEC schools, [ Select ] ["regardless of the coach salary", "assuming the same coach salary"] . At non-SEC schools, bonuses [ Select ] ["decrease", "increase"] at a rate of [ Select ] ["$600,000", "$490,000", "$40,000", "$150,000", "$1,330,000"] for a $1 million-increase in salary. The model intercept estimate suggests that if a non-SEC coach somehow earned a $0 salary, we'd expect their max bonus to equal [ Select ] ["$1,290,000", "$1,330,000", "$450,000", "$150,000", "$340,000"] .

blanks.label: higher
assumingSalary
increase

name: multiple_choice: What factors predict how much money a film will…
questionText: What factors predict how much money a film will earn? A data scientist at a top movie studio fits a multiple regression model to predict domestic Gross earnings ($ millions) from: the film Budget ($ millions), the film Run Time (minutes) average Rotten Tomatoes Rating score [0, 100] Gross = -27 + (1.1 * Budget) - (0.43 * RunTime) + (2.6 * Rating) + error Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of the beta slope coefficient for Rating? (1) An estimated slope for a partial relationship. (2) The change that we expect to see in Gross earnings for a one-point increase in a film's Rotten Tomatoes Rating if we compare films with different Ratings but with the same Budget and RunTime. (3) We expect Gross earnings to increase by $2.6 million for every one-point increase in a film's Rotten Tomatoes Rating, after adjusting for the concurrent effects of Budget and Run Time on earnings.

questionText: For a regression model: y=b0+b1∗x1+ei with a dummy variable (0 or 1) predictor x, the coefficient b1 may be interpreted as:

choices.label: A
choices.text: the predicted value of the outcome variable when the dummy variable is equal to 0.

choices.label: B
choices.text: the differential effect on the outcome variable of having the dummy variable equal to 1, rather than 0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: the predicted value of the outcome variable when the dummy variable is equal to 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: the improvement in R-squared that we get from including x in the model.

name: numerical: The data set in cars.csv includes information on the…
questionText: The data set in cars.csv includes information on the gas mileage of virtually every model of vehicle offered for sale to U.S. consumers during 2020. You will fit a regression model to predict city fuel economy in miles per gallon (city variable) in terms of the following predictor variables: powertrain -- vehicle powertrain type: Diesel, EV, FFV, Gasoline, Hybrid, or Plug-in Hybrid category -- vehicle type: Car, Small Car, SUV/Van, Truck, Two-seater, or Wagon What does the model predict for the expected city miles-per-gallon for a vehicle of the category SUV/Van with a Hybrid powertrain? Round your answer to the nearest mile-per-gallon.

name: multiple_dropdowns: This question revisits the data on video-game reaction time…
questionText: This question revisits the data on video-game reaction time that we analyzed in class and in Lesson 14. Specifically, we'll consider three variables from this data set (two that we looked at before, and one that we didn't): PictureTarget.RT: the subject's reaction time in milliseconds when presented with a visual stimulus FarAway: a dummy variable for whether the stimulus (i.e. the “bad guy” popping up on the screen) was near (0) or far away (1) within the visual scene. SceneLetter: a letter code (b, c, d, e, or f) indicating which of five scenes the subject was presented with. (Note: the letters start at b; there is no scene a in this data set) Consider the following model and its corresponding regression table: lm(PictureTarget.RT ~ FarAway + SceneLetter, data=rxntime) %>% get_regression_table() %>% select(-std_error, -statistic, -p_value) Based on this model output, which of the following statements is/are accurate? When the stimulus is far away, we expect [ Select ] ["a decrease", "an increase"] in reaction time of at least approximately [ Select ] ["50", "38", "62"] milliseconds (with 95% confidence, adjusting for the scene). [ Select ] ["Scene f", "Scene b", "Scene e", "Scene d", "Scene c"] is associated with the slowest reaction time, on average. [ Select ] ["Scene f", "Scene b", "Scene e", "Scene c", "Scene d"] is associated with the fastest reaction time, on average. When the stimulus is near, average reaction time for scene b is not more than [ Select ] ["458", "473", "488"] milliseconds (with 95% confidence).

blanks.label: an_increase
SceneE
SceneB
When the stimulus is near, average reaction time for scene b is not more than milliseconds (with 95% confidence).

name: matching: The georgia.csv file contains Georgia’s county-level voting data from…
questionText: The georgia.csv file contains Georgia’s county-level voting data from the 2000 presidential election. The 2000 election was among the most controversial in history; it turned on an esoteric set of issues surrounding voting machines and vote counts, and wasn't finally resolved until the Supreme Court's ruling in Bush v. Gore. For our purposes, the relevant variables are: votes: number of votes recorded ballots: number of ballots cast equipment: indicator for whether county used Optical scan voting machines or else Other equipment urban: indicator for whether county is predominantly Urban or Rural based on population density Use the mutate() function to define a new variable called ucountPct: ucountPct=(ballots−votes)/ballots measuring the percentage of ballots in a county that were "undercounted" or "spoiled", (i.e., ballots cast where no legal vote was recorded because the machine could not read the vote). Was there a difference, on average, in undercount percentages between Urban counties versus Rural counties? Use these variables, along with a large-sample 95% confidence interval, to evaluate the following statements:

blanks.label: In the sample, the undercount rate was higher in Rural counties.
The difference in means is not statistically significant with 95% confidence.
With 95% confidence, the undercount rate is at most around 2% lower in Urban counties.
In the sample, the undercount rate was higher in Urban counties.
The difference in means is statistically significant with 95% confidence.

name: matching: The rentals.csv data frame contains data on 98 short-term…
questionText: The rentals.csv data frame contains data on 98 short-term rentals in Santa Fe, New Mexico, including a variable for the number of listed Amenities (e.g., pool, laundry room, fireplace) on the webpage for each rental. Calculate the observed sample mean, as well a large-sample 95% confidence interval for the average number of rental property Amenities in the population. Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of this analysis? Select TRUE or FALSE for each option below.

blanks.label: We are 95% confident that the mean number of amenities in this population of rental properties is approximately 23.5.
In this population, 95% of short-term rentals will have between approximately 21 to 26 listed amenities.
We are 95% confident that the population mean may be found in the range of values represented by this interval.

If we were to take repeated random samples of the same number of rentals using the same data-generating process, and then construct a confidence interval for each of these samples, we'd expect that 95% of those intervals would contain the population mean.

name: multiple_choice: A confidence interval using de Moivre's equation is valid…
questionText: A confidence interval using de Moivre's equation is valid if which of the following conditions is true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: We are calculating a confidence interval for a population proportion based on a sample proportion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We are calculating a confidence interval for a coefficient in a regression model based on a sample model estimate.

name: multiple_choice: During 2023, the UT Athletic Director's data science team…
questionText: During 2023, the UT Athletic Director's data science team sent a well-designed survey to a large group of alumni who have in the past purchased season tickets for Longhorns athletics. Their objective was to estimate the proportion of contributing alumni who supported early withdrawal from the Big 12 Conference in the following athletic year. After data collection, they observed that 371 respondents in a random sample of 525 alumni indicated yes in support of the plan for early withdrawal. Which of the following is true of the results of this analysis? Choose the best answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sampling distribution in this context is the distribution of sample proportions that we'd expect to see if it were possible to repeatedly administer this same survey to random samples of 525 alumni.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sampling variability means that a different sample from the same population would likely produce exactly the same sample proportion.

name: multiple_choice: A sociologist uses data from the General Social Survey…
questionText: A sociologist uses data from the General Social Survey to estimate the typical "occupational prestige factor" of professions of U.S. adult residents. The survey includes a variable called Prestige, a numerical scale 0-100 for job prestige attempting to measure the level of respect/admiration for the job in society. In the sample, survey respondents' have a median prestige score of 45.1. The sociologist uses bootstrapping to calculate a 95% confidence interval for the population median prestige score: (44, 46) Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of this analysis? Choose the best answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: We are 95% confident that between 44% -- 46% of U.S. adults have a prestige score association with their occupation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We are 95% confident that the true median prestige score for U.S. adults is 45.1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: We are confident that 95% of all U.S. adults have an occupation with a prestige score between 44 and 46.

choices.label: D
choices.text: We are 95% confident that the interval 44-46 contains the true median prestige score for U.S. adults.

choices.label: B

name: multiple_choice: Which of the following statements is accurate with respect…
questionText: Which of the following statements is accurate with respect to sampling distributions? (1) A sampling distribution is the theoretical distribution of sample estimates across many repeated samples. (2) A sampling distribution represents the results of a thought experiment: specifically, how much your answer might change from one sample to the next under the same random process that generated your data. (3) The sampling variability that we observe in some summary statistic is not a characteristic of the particular sample from which that statistic was calculated, but rather associated with the sample-generating procedure.
